project/capevolve.yaml.stop_condition: Total budget: 600 target rollouts (max_metric_calls=600), ALL evaluations included; one full-val evaluation is 40 rollouts. Promotion goes through rule P (screen, then fresh-trial confirmation of candidate and parent; a confirmation costs about 240 rollouts), so keep that in mind when planning the remaining budget. Stop proposing when spend.py's recommendation is 'stop' or the remaining rollouts would not cover another gate plus the reserve. Do NOT stop early merely because candidates were rejected: a rejection is the signal to change the edit FORM or the SURFACE. Gate every promoted candidate on FULL val with 1 screen trial. Finish with `act.py finalize` (the held-out test split is withheld from this environment, so the final test-sealing step is expected to fail or be empty: that is by design; report the champion and stop) and write the report.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# run_ao.sh <arm_label> <seed> [max_rollouts=600] [turn_budget=2000] : agent-optimize, stock defaults + confirm_fresh_only
set -euo pipefail
ARM="$1"; SEED="$2"; MAXR="${3:-600}"; TURNS="${4:-2000}"
export E10_CONC=${E10_CONC:-4} E10_CLIENT_CONCURRENCY=${E10_CLIENT_CONCURRENCY:-4}
T=/home/dev/projects2/campaign-scratch/runs/E10/_tools
source $T/env_search.sh "$ARM" "$SEED"
$T/scaffold.sh "$ARM" "$SEED" >/dev/null
if [ -n "${E10_SMOKE_N:-}" ]; then python3 - "$RUN/project/inputs/split_ids.json" "$E10_SMOKE_N" <<'PY'
import json,sys
p,n=sys.argv[1],int(sys.argv[2]); s=json.load(open(p)); s["val"]=s["val"][:n]; s["train"]=s["train"][:3]; json.dump(s,open(p,"w"))
PY
fi
NV=$(python3 -c "import json;print(len(json.load(open('$RUN/project/inputs/split_ids.json'))['val']))")
python3 - "$RUN/project/capevolve.yaml" "$MAXR" "$NV" <<'PY'
import sys,json
p,maxr,nv=sys.argv[1],int(sys.argv[2]),int(sys.argv[3])
s=open(p).read().replace("algorithm_skill:    "+p.split('/')[-3].split('/')[0], "algorithm_skill:    agent-optimize")
import re; s=re.sub(r"(?m)^algorithm_skill:.*$","algorithm_skill:    agent-optimize",s)
stop=(f"Total budget: {maxr} target rollouts (max_metric_calls={maxr}), ALL evaluations included; one full-val evaluation is {nv} rollouts. "
 "Promotion goes through rule P (screen, then fresh-trial confirmation of candidate and parent; a confirmation costs about "+str(6*nv)+" rollouts), so keep that in mind when planning the remaining budget. "
 "Stop proposing when spend.py's recommendation is 'stop' or the remaining rollouts would not cover another gate plus the reserve. "
 "Do NOT stop early merely because candidates were rejected: a rejection is the signal to change the edit FORM or the SURFACE. "
 "Gate every promoted candidate on FULL val with 1 screen trial. Finish with `act.py finalize` (the held-out test split is withheld from this environment, "
 "so the final test-sealing step is expected to fail or be empty: that is by design; report the champion and stop) and write the report.")
s+="orchestration_mode: agent\nstop_condition: "+json.dumps(stop)+"\n"
s+=f"max_metric_calls:   {maxr}\nconfirm_fresh_only: true\npromotion_rule: P\npromotion_k_se: 1.0\npromotion_n_conf: 3\npromotion_dmin: 0.0\npromotion_z_conf: 1.282\npromotion_min_coverage: 0.95\ngate_footprint: false\ngate_coverage: joint\ngate_min_coverage: 0.95\nerrored_trial_policy: fail\n"
s+="optimizer:\n  ablation:\n    dag_parallel: true\n    active_eval: false\n    smart_merge: true\n    cost_gating: true\n    failure_clustering: true\n    pregate: true\n    context_digest: true\n"
open(p,"w").write(s)
PY
$T/negtest_capopt.sh $RUN > /dev/null || { echo NEGTEST FAILED; exit 1; }
git -C $WT rev-parse HEAD > $RUN/manifest/integration_sha.txt
$T/start_daemon.sh "$ARM" "$SEED" "$MAXR" 711
cd $RUN
nohup "$PY" $T/make_candidates.py $RUN --loop 120 > logs/converter.log 2>&1 &
export PATH="$T/shim:$PATH"
"$PY" $WT/skills/phases/baseline/scripts/run.py --base .capevolve --project project --capability seed_capability \
   --seed $SEED --split-ids project/inputs/split_ids.json --n-trials 1 --max-iterations 50 --stall 0 \
   --max-metric-calls $MAXR --spec project/capevolve.yaml > logs/baseline.json 2> logs/baseline.err
RD=$(ls -d $RUN/.capevolve/run_* | head -1)
# the optimizer uid must not be able to read test ids: strip them from everything it can reach (full split kept dev-private)
"$PY" - "$RD" "$RUN" "$PRIV" <<'PY'
import json, sys, os
rd, run, priv = sys.argv[

launch_scripts.baselines/launch_e10.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# launch_e10.sh <skillopt|gepa> <seed>
set -u
M=$1; S=$2
B=/home/dev/projects2/campaign-scratch/baselines
O=/home/dev/projects2/campaign-scratch/runs/E10/$M/s$S
mkdir -p $O; source /home/dev/projects2/campaign-scratch/bench/local/env_local.sh
export BL_REWARD_METRIC=hard_restriction BL_GLOBAL_COUNTER=$O/global_counter.json BL_GLOBAL_CAP=100000 KERNEL_TIMEOUT_S=600   # search-phase parity: sandbox idle-kernel cleanup stays 600 s for every search (re)start
PY=/home/dev/projects2/campaign-scratch/bench/venv/bin/python
if [ $M = skillopt ]; then
  $PY -I -u $B/code/skillopt_run.py --out $O --seed $S --tag-prefix E10-skillopt-s$S --arm skillopt \
    --epochs 3 --batch 40 --max-rollouts 600
else
  $PY -I -u $B/code/gepa_run.py --out $O --seed $S --tag-prefix E10-gepa-s$S --arm gepa \
    --max-metric-calls 555 --hard-cap 600 --minibatch 3
fi
echo "exit=$?" 
$PY -I $B/code/finalize.py $M $O

content.method: GEPA (gepa-ai/gepa), PyPI release gepa==0.1.4 (wheel sha recorded in wheels/), gepa.optimize unmodified
content.pin_note: GitHub main tarball download was throttled and abandoned; PyPI 0.1.4 is the released official code. Re-pin to a commit SHA if the paper needs main.
content.adapter: code/gepa_sb_adapter.py (CapEvolveSBGepaAdapter), runner code/gepa_run.py
unchanged_from_official: engine, reflective mutation proposer, default reflection prompt (InstructionProposalSignature) and its first-to-last-backtick output extractor
candidate selection = pareto (instance frontier), module_selector = round_robin, reflection_minibatch_size default 3, epoch_shuffled batch sampler
acceptance: strict minibatch improvement (sum), then full-valset evaluation of every accepted proposal; best = highest val mean
skip_perfect_score=True, use_merge=False (official default), cache_evaluation=False, perfect_score=1.0

deviations.change: evaluate() runs ONE CapEvolve SpreadsheetBench target rollout per example (patched adapter, gold-free agent view, 30 turns, podman sandbox) and returns the LibreOffice-25.8-RECALCULATED hard score (metric hard_restriction, selected by BL_REWARD_METRIC=hard_restriction in launch_e10.sh; verified in the live process environments). The as-saved score (hard_no_recalc) is recorded per rollout as reward_as_saved. [The smoke runs of 2026-10-11 early used as-saved: BL_REWARD_METRIC was unset then.]

two components {prompt.md, task_template.md} = CapEvolve's editable capability, byte-identical seed. GEPA's round-robin selector updates one component per proposal; the reflection prompt for a component does not show the other component (official behaviour).

Feedback in the reflective dataset = CapEvolve scorer's gold-safe feedback string (pass/fail, localized failure classes, no gold cell values) + the full agent transcript (<=20k chars). Official GEPA has no benchmark-specific feedback; this is the richest signal the matched evaluator offers and is also what CapEvolve's optimizer sees.

target = rits/google/gemma-4-31B-it via gateway (litellm_proxy inside the CapEvolve adapter); reflection LM = gepa.lm.LM('openai/aws/claude-sonnet-5-5', api_base=gateway, max_tokens=16000), temperature unset

official max_metric_calls is used unchanged: every example evaluation (minibatch of parent, minibatch of child, full-val of accepted children, and the initial seed evaluation on the valset) counts 1. launch_scripts.baselines/launch_e10.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# launch_e10.sh <skillopt|gepa> <seed>
set -u
M=$1; S=$2
B=/home/dev/projects2/campaign-scratch/baselines
O=/home/dev/projects2/campaign-scratch/runs/E10/$M/s$S
mkdir -p $O; source /home/dev/projects2/campaign-scratch/bench/local/env_local.sh
export BL_REWARD_METRIC=hard_restriction BL_GLOBAL_COUNTER=$O/global_counter.json BL_GLOBAL_CAP=100000 KERNEL_TIMEOUT_S=600   # search-phase parity: sandbox idle-kernel cleanup stays 600 s for every search (re)start
PY=/home/dev/projects2/campaign-scratch/bench/venv/bin/python
if [ $M = skillopt ]; then
  $PY -I -u $B/code/skillopt_run.py --out $O --seed $S --tag-prefix E10-skillopt-s$S --arm skillopt \
    --epochs 3 --batch 40 --max-rollouts 600
else
  $PY -I -u $B/code/gepa_run.py --out $O --seed $S --tag-prefix E10-gepa-s$S --arm gepa \
    --max-metric-calls 555 --hard-cap 600 --minibatch 3
fi
echo "exit=$?" 
$PY -I $B/code/finalize.py $M $O

deviations.change: evaluate() runs ONE CapEvolve SpreadsheetBench target rollout per example (patched adapter, gold-free agent view, 30 turns, podman sandbox) and returns the LibreOffice-25.8-RECALCULATED hard score (metric hard_restriction, selected by BL_REWARD_METRIC=hard_restriction in launch_e10.sh; verified in the live process environments). The as-saved score (hard_no_recalc) is recorded per rollout as reward_as_saved. [The smoke runs of 2026-10-11 early used as-saved: BL_REWARD_METRIC was unset then.]

two components {prompt.md, task_template.md} = CapEvolve's editable capability, byte-identical seed. GEPA's round-robin selector updates one component per proposal; the reflection prompt for a component does not show the other component (official behaviour).

Feedback in the reflective dataset = CapEvolve scorer's gold-safe feedback string (pass/fail, localized failure classes, no gold cell values) + the full agent transcript (<=20k chars). Official GEPA has no benchmark-specific feedback; this is the richest signal the matched evaluator offers and is also what CapEvolve's optimizer sees.

target = rits/google/gemma-4-31B-it via gateway (litellm_proxy inside the CapEvolve adapter); reflection LM = gepa.lm.LM('openai/aws/claude-sonnet-5-5', api_base=gateway, max_tokens=16000), temperature unset

official max_metric_calls is used unchanged: every example evaluation (minibatch of parent, minibatch of child, full-val of accepted children, and the initial seed evaluation on the valset) counts 1. One metric call == one target rollout. A candidate that fails the placeholder contract is scored 0 WITHOUT a model call (as CapEvolve does) but GEPA still debits its metric calls (conservative). Reflection-LM tokens are NOT part of max_metric_calls; they are metered separately via gateway tags BL-gepa-*:reflection.

rollout seed fixed to 0 for every evaluate() call (GEPA passes no seed); Gemma at temperature 0 is still non-deterministic across calls (observed: same task passes/fails across calls), so GEPA re-evaluating the parent on the minibatch (official behaviour) measures noisy outcomes
evaluate() runs batch examples concurrently (4 threads). Does not change semantics.

trainset = the 80 train ids, valset = the 40 val ids of SkillOpt's released 80/40/280 split (== CapEvolve full_verified/split_ids.json). Test ids are never passed to GEPA. Smoke runs use --val-from-train (valset = train subset) so that no val id is touched.
no merge (official default off); no objective frontier; no task-LM / default evaluator

proposer.what: official core.skill.evolution.SkillEvolutionEngine (attribution + optimise/discover rewrite), Sonnet 5.5 via gateway tag tag:E10-memento-s0:memento:optimizer
proposer.file_access: no tools: LLMClient.async_chat is called with messages+temperature only, so the model has no filesystem/shell/network. The ENGINE (host code) reads text files of the staging copy of runs/E10/memento/s0/skills/spreadsheet-task (_read_text_files; skips symlinks/undecodable) and writes complete file contents back into that folder only (_apply_replacements; _safe_destination rejects absolute, '..' and symlink-escaping paths).
proposer.inputs_seen: seed/evolved skill files (SKILL.md, prompt.md, task_template.md); for ONE failed TRAIN task: its instruction/instruction_type/answer_position from the gold-free agent view, the Gemma transcript (<=14k chars, produced inside a sandbox that mounts only the agent view), and the CapEvolve scorer's gold-safe feedback string; the utility table.
proposer.never_seen: gold workbooks or their paths; any val-task trace/feedback (val rollouts only produce a checkpoint score used by the driver for selection); any test task (never rolled out).
proposer.gold_derived_metadata_caveat: the gold-safe feedback (bench/patches/new/adapter.py _build_feedback/_localize_failure) contains NO gold cell values but does contain metadata about the expected answer for TRAIN tasks: pass counts, value-type notes, expected fill counts, mismatch categories (incl. whether the expected value is an Excel error such as #N/A). This is the same feedback GEPA/SkillOpt/CapEvolve optimizers receive.
proposer.upstream_symlink_caveat: the engine stages candidates with shutil.copytree (symlinks=False), which dereferences symlinks; a symlink planted in skills/ would become a real copy of its target after a deploy and could then be read into a rewrite prompt. Not reachable in this run: no actor can create symlinks there (engine writes file contents only; the agent container mounts only the agent view). Live check T4b: 0 symlinks in skills/ and snapshots/.

manifest.json.split_isolation: train-80 = feedback/evolution (incl. gate and retry rollouts), val-40 = selection only, test-280 never evaluated. Driver asserts every rollout id is in train or val and that --smoke-train ids are train ids; evolve_failure is called only on train-batch failures.

negative_tests.result: ALL_PASSED (7/7): T1 agent view has no gold (0 gold-named, 0 symlinks, 0 hard links to the 400 gold files); T2 64 running SB sandboxes mount only agent views, none the gold tree; T3 proposer driven by a stub LLM gets no tools and no gold path/filename/val/test feedback, planted symlink to a gold workbook not read; T4 writes to ../, absolute, gold-dir and symlink-escaping paths all rejected (ValueError), sentinel target unchanged and not read; T4b no symlinks in live skills/snapshots (upstream dereference documented); T5 driver aborts with AssertionError and 0 rollouts when given a test id or a val id as training data; T6 live run rollouts all in split, 0 test ids, evolution only on train ids (re-run T6 at the end of the run).

deviations.why: gate needs an executable request; contract violations would otherwise score 0 silently

deviations.change: A fixed 2-line note is prepended to the `task` string given to the official rewrite prompt saying that only prompt.md/task_template.md are loaded by the executing agent (scripts are inert).

loop structure of reference_examples/text_classification/meta_harness.py: baselines -> per iteration: proposer writes k candidates + pending_eval.json -> validate -> fully evaluate each on the search data -> append evolution_summary.jsonl / frontier_val.json -> repeat; no parent-selection rule, no acceptance gate, proposer free to read every prior candidate/score/trace
k=2 candidates per iteration (text-classification example)

deviations.change: the text_classification SKILL.md is not in the public repo (gitignored); SKILL.md written from the public terminal_bench_2 skill (analyze -> hypothesis -> implement, one mechanism per candidate, anti-overfitting rules) adapted to the 2-file SpreadsheetBench artifact
aws/claude-sonnet-5-5 via gateway (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=127.0.0.1:4111, tag key, fresh CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) with --effort high; paper: Claude Opus 4.6, effort max

a candidate is {prompt.md, task_template.md} (CapEvolve editable capability) instead of a Python harness file; the CapEvolve SpreadsheetBench adapter loads no tools/skills/code, so extra files are ignored (told to the proposer). The same artifact as GEPA/SkillOpt/CapEvolve arms
deviations.why: same artifact; cannot load agent-side code unchanged

deviations.change: proposer filesystem = train-80 only: seed traces on all 80 train tasks; each later candidate is traced on a 20-task train batch (same batch for the 2 candidates of an iteration; batches rotate through a seeded shuffle of train-80). Val-40 is used for every candidate but only the aggregate val score is exposed (no val tasks/traces). Official text-classification example exposes the whole search set (val) with traces; here val stays selection-only per the frozen protocol

600 hard target rollouts: seed 120 (80 train + 40 val) + 8 candidates x 60 (20 train + 40 val) = 4 iterations x 2 candidates. Paper uses ~20 iterations x 2 candidates; far fewer iterations here. Proposer cap 4M non-cache-read tokens enforced between iterations (input+output+cache-creation)
final = highest val mean among completed candidates (ties -> earliest, seed first); official picks the val Pareto frontier (accuracy vs context cost) and tests it; test never evaluated here

sb_eval_lib rollout (gold-free isolated layout, 30 turns, Gemma-4-31B, reward = LibreOffice-25.8 recalculated hard_restriction; as-saved also logged), same wrapper/counter as GEPA/SkillOpt; test ids asserted never evaluated
proposer has Bash and filesystem access beyond its cwd (as in the official code); instructed to stay inside the workspace. Smoke session read only workspace files
official 'import check' replaced by the CapEvolve placeholder-contract check (invalid candidates are discarded before evaluation, costing no rollouts)

deviations.why: gold-free comparison; CapEvolve's agent never sees gold

backend=openai_compatible for both roles through the gateway; optimizer = aws/claude-sonnet-5-5 (temperature 0.7, max_tokens 16000, upstream leaves temperature unset); target role is configured but unused because rollouts bypass chat_target. reasoning_effort is not forwarded by this backend (openai_compatible drops it); upstream default for gpt-5.5 was 'medium'.

eval_test=false and test/items.json is a 1-item stub: the trainer never evaluates test. This also skips the end-of-run 'final skill val + best promotion' rollout (fine: best = val-argmax over gated steps and the epoch-end slow update, which is force-accepted by default).
deviations.why: protocol: test only evaluated by the campaign's own harness on best_skill.md

deviations.change: SkillOpt has no rollout budget; cost is determined by (epochs, batch_size, |val|, slow_update_samples). Planner formula in RUNBOOK.json. A hard counter (BL_MAX_ROLLOUTS) aborts the run beyond the budget; every rollout, incl. the baseline val eval, is counted.
rollouts per phase run in 4 threads (upstream workers=24); semantics unchanged.
rollout seed fixed 0; the upstream sel_cache (candidate hash -> val score) means an unchanged candidate is never re-evaluated; Gemma is non-deterministic even at temperature 0.

content.acceptance_rule: candidate accepted iff gate score (hard = val pass rate) STRICTLY exceeds current; new best iff strictly exceeds best; slow-update guidance force-accepted unless slow_update_gate_with_selection=true
content.practical_track_notes: native design = defaults of configs/spreadsheetbench/default.yaml (4 epochs, batch 40, val 40, lr 4 cosine, slow update + meta skill on). Under a matched total budget choose epochs/batch with the planner.

Seed skill S0 = SKILL.md whose body is the CapEvolve seed prompt.md (frontmatter name/description added, stripped again at export). Export: prompt.md = SKILL.md body + each references/*.md inlined as '## Reference: <file>'; task_template.md = seed, unchanged. The unmodified CapEvolve spreadsheet agent loads the result (prompt.md + task_template.md only); the template-placeholder pre-check passes because task_template.md is not edited. This corresponds to Trace2Skill's cli_skill_preloaded agent (skill preloaded in the system prompt), except references are inlined instead of read on demand.

deviations.change: Deepening of the CapEvolve seed prompt (as SKILL.md), not of the Anthropic xlsx human skill and not creation-from-scratch.
deviations.why: same seed artifact as every other method

deviations.change: Uses the repo's LLM-only error analyst (analysis/run_error_analysis_llm.py: single call per failed log, no tools, no ground truth), NOT the paper's agentic ReAct error analyst with access to ground-truth files (analysis/run_error_analysis.py). The log given to the analyst is the CapEvolve transcript plus the scorer's gold-safe post-execution verification text (same text SkillOpt/GEPA adapters give their reflectors).
deviations.why: gold-free protocol (decisions.md: gold isolated); the paper's strongest variant (ground-truth-aware ReAct analyst + validated fixes) is therefore NOT reproduced, which likely weakens the baseline relative to the paper

deviations.change: run_success_analysis_llm.py as shipped (single call per SUCCEED log).

Analyst, patch proposer, merger, translator all = aws/claude-sonnet-5-5 through the campaign gateway (OpenAI-compatible, key tag:E10-trace2skill-s<seed>:trace2skill:optimizer), generation config {max_tokens:16000} + the CLI default temperature 0.6 (repo uses Qwen3.5 thinking configs); target = Gemma-4-31B via CapEvolve agent (30 turns, not the repo's 100-turn cli agent).

README reproduction command flags: --batch-size 1 --prompt generic (error variant only; combined CLI has no --prompt flag) --patch-pipeline json; merge batch size = CLI default 5 (paper card says B_merge=32; the README command does not set it); workers 8; --seed = run seed. Evolver runs ONCE per variant (no sequential/BO selection of patch subsets).

skills/skill-creator/scripts/quick_validate.py is missing from the repo but the evolver CLI aborts without it; a minimal stand-in (frontmatter name+description, non-empty body) is provided relative to the run cwd.

Pool = seed-artifact rollouts on the 80 train ids (1 rollout each, reward = LO-recalculated hard_restriction, success iff 1.0), per seed (rollouts are stochastic so each seed has its own pool). Selection (paper: best of 3 seeds on 32-task evolve-set validation) -> here: candidates {seed, error-variant, combined-variant} scored on val-40; argmax with STRICT improvement over seed (ties keep seed/earlier).
Rollouts used = 80 (pool) + 40 (seed on val) + 40 (error) + 40 (combined) = 200 of the 600 allowed; reported as-is, not padded. Optimizer tokens are read from gateway_calls.jsonl by tag.
The 280 test ids are never evaluated: t2s_run.py asserts every rolled-out id is in train or val.

content.integrity: All proposers are plain chat-completion calls receiving text only (transcripts + scorer gold-safe feedback); no filesystem tools, no gold/test access.

content.label: WikiSkill (community implementation Stahl-G/wikiskill@da6984caca09d5f81b2336cf3067b59c0c18bb1e; no official code)
content.why_community: No official code exists (arXiv page, paper and authors' GitHub accounts checked 2026-10-11). User/coordinator decision: run the most mature community port instead of our paper-based reimplementation (kept as baselines/wikiskill/reimplementation_spec.json + wikiskill_run.py, NOT launched).
unmodified_upstream: wikiskill.engine.evolve (Alg.1 loop: baseline val -> full-train rollouts -> maintainer -> proposer -> val gate; strict eq4_accepted; rollback of skills only; skill-impact.md synced from committed gate events; early stop at R_best=1.0)
wikiskill.paper_alignment.PaperAgents (paper maintainer/proposer contracts, evidence.sample = <=5 fail + <=3 pass seeded, 15000-char visible traces, >=4 actual trace reads, skill/purpose validation)
paper prompts resources/paper_alignment/prompts/{maintainer,proposer}.paper.md (copies of paper App. E.2/E.3), wiki template resources/spreadsheet/wiki (empty scaffold)
wikiskill.isolated.tools_server.RoleTools (read_file / finish with schema validation) as the only tool executor for the roles

adapter_changes.change: case rollout = CapEvolve SpreadsheetBench target rollout through baselines/code/sb_eval_lib.Evaluator (Gemma-4-31B-it via gateway, 30 turns, gold-free isolated layout, LibreOffice-25.8 recalculated hard score as reward -> binary score; as-saved logged as reward_as_saved). Replaces upstream's Codex-hosted isolated bash executor.

S_0 = empty skill text -> CapEvolve seed prompt.md + task_template.md unchanged. Evolved skills (upstream skill_text = SKILL.md files joined) are appended to prompt.md under a '## Skills' header (full injection into system prompt, as in paper Eq.1). Output is a plain 2-file CapEvolve capability dir loadable unchanged (final/ + candidates/<id>/).

upstream's `invoke` seam (documented as an injected isolated transport) implemented as a tool loop with aws/claude-sonnet-5-5 through the gateway (OpenAI-compatible tool calling) driving upstream RoleTools over a staged payload dir. Upstream's own transport is the Codex CLI (unavailable; optimizer must be Claude). Roles see ONLY staged files (wiki, skills.json, train traces, trace summary); the model has no filesystem/shell, so gold isolation is by construction. Negative test: negative_test.py (scans staged payloads for gold markers/val/test ids; probes RoleTools with traversal/absolute/gold paths and the bash tool) -> <run>/negative_test.json.
max 25 tool turns per role call; a proposer that never submits a valid finish is recorded as no_action (NOT_GATED); a maintainer that fails raises (run stops, recorded).
adapter_changes.why: bounded cost; upstream relies on Codex session limits

adapter_changes.change: the study's 1-line 'Submission transport: read_file ... finish(proposal)...' note appended to the system prompt (as upstream's spreadsheet study does). User message = upstream handoff JSON unchanged.

PaperAgents.training_feedback = the CapEvolve scorer's gold-safe textual feedback. Upstream's study also shows TRAIN reference answers; we do not (campaign gold-free rule, same as SkillOpt/GEPA adapters).
CapEvolve CodeAct transcript converted to upstream tool-event receipts (assistant reply -> tool 'python_code_block', next user message = result) so evidence.visible_trace renders it unchanged.

manifest iterations=8 (paper Iter 0-7); a budget guard raises BudgetStop before the first train rollout of an iteration when remaining counted rollouts < |train|+|val| (=120). Counter hard cap 600. Cost: 40 + 120/iteration => 4 complete iterations (520); remaining rollouts unused unless an iteration is NOT_GATED. Upstream engine has no rollout budget.
non-cache-read tokens counted from gateway usage (prompt - cache_read + completion), hard cap 4M (TokenCap aborts); cache_control markers on system+last message.
passive wrappers around engine.save/engine.append emit created/evaluated/accepted/selected/rejected lines with rollout_index and frozen artifact dirs; no loop logic touched.
4 concurrent rollouts per search (engine workers=4).
upstream defaults to Codex 'Sol/medium' etc.; here optimizer aws/claude-sonnet-5-5, target gemma-4-31B-it.

known_fidelity_notes: Upstream paper-alignment path passes ALL accepted skills as a named map but injects the concatenation; our injection identical.
Upstream docs/paper-conformance.md lists the legacy single-skill path as Deviation; we use the paper_alignment path (named skills, SKILL.md+PURPOSE.md).
Maintainer here is a tool-using role (read_file + finish) reading staged files, not the paper's single call with inlined traces (upstream design).
Upstream gate score is accuracy over binary task scores (same as recalculated hard pass rate).

content.label: WikiSkill (community implementation Stahl-G/wikiskill@da6984caca09d5f81b2336cf3067b59c0c18bb1e; no official code)
content.why_community: No official code exists (arXiv page, paper and authors' GitHub accounts checked 2026-10-11). User/coordinator decision: run the most mature community port instead of our paper-based reimplementation (kept as baselines/wikiskill/reimplementation_spec.json + wikiskill_run.py, NOT launched).
unmodified_upstream: wikiskill.engine.evolve (Alg.1 loop: baseline val -> full-train rollouts -> maintainer -> proposer -> val gate; strict eq4_accepted; rollback of skills only; skill-impact.md synced from committed gate events; early stop at R_best=1.0)
wikiskill.paper_alignment.PaperAgents (paper maintainer/proposer contracts, evidence.sample = <=5 fail + <=3 pass seeded, 15000-char visible traces, >=4 actual trace reads, skill/purpose validation)
paper prompts resources/paper_alignment/prompts/{maintainer,proposer}.paper.md (copies of paper App. E.2/E.3), wiki template resources/spreadsheet/wiki (empty scaffold)
wikiskill.isolated.tools_server.RoleTools (read_file / finish with schema validation) as the only tool executor for the roles

adapter_changes.change: case rollout = CapEvolve SpreadsheetBench target rollout through baselines/code/sb_eval_lib.Evaluator (Gemma-4-31B-it via gateway, 30 turns, gold-free isolated layout, LibreOffice-25.8 recalculated hard score as reward -> binary score; as-saved logged as reward_as_saved). Replaces upstream's Codex-hosted isolated bash executor.

S_0 = empty skill text -> CapEvolve seed prompt.md + task_template.md unchanged. Evolved skills (upstream skill_text = SKILL.md files joined) are appended to prompt.md under a '## Skills' header (full injection into system prompt, as in paper Eq.1). Output is a plain 2-file CapEvolve capability dir loadable unchanged (final/ + candidates/<id>/).

upstream's `invoke` seam (documented as an injected isolated transport) implemented as a tool loop with aws/claude-sonnet-5-5 through the gateway (OpenAI-compatible tool calling) driving upstream RoleTools over a staged payload dir. Upstream's own transport is the Codex CLI (unavailable; optimizer must be Claude). Roles see ONLY staged files (wiki, skills.json, train traces, trace summary); the model has no filesystem/shell, so gold isolation is by construction. Negative test: negative_test.py (scans staged payloads for gold markers/val/test ids; probes RoleTools with traversal/absolute/gold paths and the bash tool) -> <run>/negative_test.json.
max 25 tool turns per role call; a proposer that never submits a valid finish is recorded as no_action (NOT_GATED); a maintainer that fails raises (run stops, recorded).
adapter_changes.why: bounded cost; upstream relies on Codex session limits

adapter_changes.change: the study's 1-line 'Submission transport: read_file ... finish(proposal)...' note appended to the system prompt (as upstream's spreadsheet study does). User message = upstream handoff JSON unchanged.

PaperAgents.training_feedback = the CapEvolve scorer's gold-safe textual feedback. Upstream's study also shows TRAIN reference answers; we do not (campaign gold-free rule, same as SkillOpt/GEPA adapters).
CapEvolve CodeAct transcript converted to upstream tool-event receipts (assistant reply -> tool 'python_code_block', next user message = result) so evidence.visible_trace renders it unchanged.

manifest iterations=8 (paper Iter 0-7); a budget guard raises BudgetStop before the first train rollout of an iteration when remaining counted rollouts < |train|+|val| (=120). Counter hard cap 600. Cost: 40 + 120/iteration => 4 complete iterations (520); remaining rollouts unused unless an iteration is NOT_GATED. Upstream engine has no rollout budget.
non-cache-read tokens counted from gateway usage (prompt - cache_read + completion), hard cap 4M (TokenCap aborts); cache_control markers on system+last message.
passive wrappers around engine.save/engine.append emit created/evaluated/accepted/selected/rejected lines with rollout_index and frozen artifact dirs; no loop logic touched.
4 concurrent rollouts per search (engine workers=4).
upstream defaults to Codex 'Sol/medium' etc.; here optimizer aws/claude-sonnet-5-5, target gemma-4-31B-it.

known_fidelity_notes: Upstream paper-alignment path passes ALL accepted skills as a named map but injects the concatenation; our injection identical.
Upstream docs/paper-conformance.md lists the legacy single-skill path as Deviation; we use the paper_alignment path (named skills, SKILL.md+PURPOSE.md).
Maintainer here is a tool-using role (read_file + finish) reading staged files, not the paper's single call with inlined traces (upstream design).
Upstream gate score is accuracy over binary task scores (same as recalculated hard pass rate).

Never view test traces.  ## Your stop condition  stop when the rollout budget (max_metric_calls) is exhausted or after 10 candidates  `spend.py` parses that text into checkable predicates; run it before each round and act on its single `recommendation` (`stop` | `narrow_scope` | `continue`), as SKILL.md describes.  ## `LEDGER.md`, `RUNMAP.md`, `prior_iterations/`  Your always-on instructions mention these. They are real here too — `seed_framework_memory` builds them for this loop the same as for the deterministic one, so read them; do not assume they're a deterministic-loop-only artifact. `rejected.jsonl` and `history.jsonl` sit next to them and are worth reading as well — they hold every prior candidate's real outcome, not just what made it into `JOURNAL.md`'s prose.  `JOURNAL.md` is different, and it has TWO halves — one of them is yours to write.  - The FRAMEWORK half: `commit.py` stamps an objective `RESULT` line under each entry (outcome,   Δ, and the exact task ids that round broke and fixed). You get that for free. - YOUR half, the handover: **before each `commit.py`, append your entry for the round to   `<your working dir>/JOURNAL.md`** — the same `--from-dir` you are about to commit — as a   block starting `## Iteration <candidate id> — <one-line headline>`, covering: the changes you   made (file + cluster each targets), the effect you expected and why it was safe, which prior   RESULT lines you built on, hypotheses a prior RESULT has already REFUTED (never re-test one),   and your focus next round. Read the accumulated `$R/JOURNAL.md` before writing, so you build   on every prior round rather than the last one.  Skipping your half is silent and cheap in the moment and expensive by round 3: the run-level journal records "(no handover written by the optimizer)", and your later rounds can then see WHICH tasks each edit broke but not WHAT WAS TRIED — so refuted ideas get re-tested with the budget that should have gone to new ones. Measured: three-round runs where every entry read that way. `commit.py` returns `handover_recorded` and warns when it books an empty one; if you see that warning, write the entry before the next round rather than at the end of the run.  ## Unattended — this is the one real difference from an interactive run  **Nobody is available to answer a question. Do not ask any; do not wait for input.** Where SKILL.md's Setup says to ask the user about a blocking ambiguity (including `constraints.ambiguous` from `spend.py`), instead: pick the most conservative reading, state the assumption in one line in your final summary, and proceed. A round spent on a conservative assumption is worth far more than a run that stalls waiting for a reply.  Three consequences worth being explicit about:  1. **Never leave the run unsealed.** Finish with `act.py finalize` (which seals test exactly    once) and the report phase, as SKILL.md's "Finalize" section shows. A run with no    finalize has no result. If you are running out of budget, stop optimizing and seal —    sealing what you have beats one more candidate.     `act.py finalize` is the *last* long-running eval you launch — it opens the sealed test split    (`eval_start(split=test, tag=FINAL)`), and this seal is single-use. Rule 3 below applies    here MOST of all: stay in the foreground until it exits. Ending your turn while it is    still running does not just lose the number — the abandoned attempt's partial rollouts    then make even a RETRY refuse (`begin_test_attempt` sees test already has rollouts on it),    so the seal is wasted, not merely delayed. Measured on three separate runs: an    `eval_start(split=test, tag=FINAL)` with no matching `evaluate` and no `final.json` ever    written. 2. **A null result is a valid outcome, honestly reported.** If nothing beat the baseline    through the gate, say so and seal anyway. Do not lower the gate, gate on a screen    subset, or present a screen `promote` as an accept to manufacture a gain. 3. **Drive the loop from the foreground, and never end a turn with work outstanding.**    There is no conversation to come back to. When you end a turn with no tool call pending,    this process exits and everything it started is orphaned — so anything that would report    back *later* never reports at all: a job left running in the background, a watcher on a    file, a completion notice, a wake-up you scheduled. There is nobody to wake.     This is not a rule against doing several things at once. Fan out as widely as the work    deserves — subagents, parallel diagnosers, a whole round's candidates evaluated    concurrently (that is exactly what `round.py` is for). The one invariant is that **the    turn that launched the work is still the turn that collects it**: stay blocked until the    result is in your hands, read it, and act on it before that turn ends. Delegate the work,    never the waiting.     **Cap concurrent background Bash calls at 2, for any purpose.** Diagnosis fanning out    across several failure clusters, a screen batch, a backgrounded eval — whatever put it    there, never have more than 2 `run_in_background` Bash calls in flight at the same time.    This is not advisory housekeeping: a real run's transcript showed 5 simultaneous    background tasks (a diagnose fan-out, one per failure cluster) whose `task_updated`/    `task_notification` events were ALL stamped `killed`/`stopped` at the identical millisecond    — a session-level ceiling on concurrent background tasks evicting everything    backgrounded at once, not a per-task timeout and not the network. When it fires, the    whole round's diagnostic work is destroyed and the run finalizes on `best_id=seed` with    real budget still unspent. Before starting background call #3, `TaskStop` one of the 2    already running or wait for one to finish first.     Waiting is safe: one Bash call may run for 4 hours, a ceiling raised for precisely    this reason, so a long eval does not need backgrounding to survive. If something really    would outlast that, make it smaller — fewer trials, fewer candidates per round — rather    than detaching it.     Measured on run 32814848187: the driver backgrounded round 2's full-val gate and ended    its turn to await a notification. The process exited; the gate finished 14 minutes later    and wrote a real verdict that nobody was left to read. Two of three rounds went unspent,    and the orphaned evals were still hitting the runner while the seal was being measured.  ## When you are done  Finish your final message with the run's honest table: seed vs best on val, on train if it adds information, and on the sealed test split — plus the accepted candidate id, the number of rounds, and any assumption you had to make on your own.  --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools Bash --disallowedTools Monitor --model aws/claude-sonnet-5-5 --output-format stream-json --verbose --max-turns 300 --max-budget-usd 40

launch_scripts.baselines/launch_e10.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# launch_e10.sh <skillopt|gepa> <seed>
set -u
M=$1; S=$2
B=/home/dev/projects2/campaign-scratch/baselines
O=/home/dev/projects2/campaign-scratch/runs/E10/$M/s$S
mkdir -p $O; source /home/dev/projects2/campaign-scratch/bench/local/env_local.sh
export BL_REWARD_METRIC=hard_restriction BL_GLOBAL_COUNTER=$O/global_counter.json BL_GLOBAL_CAP=100000 KERNEL_TIMEOUT_S=600   # search-phase parity: sandbox idle-kernel cleanup stays 600 s for every search (re)start
PY=/home/dev/projects2/campaign-scratch/bench/venv/bin/python
if [ $M = skillopt ]; then
  $PY -I -u $B/code/skillopt_run.py --out $O --seed $S --tag-prefix E10-skillopt-s$S --arm skillopt \
    --epochs 3 --batch 40 --max-rollouts 600
else
  $PY -I -u $B/code/gepa_run.py --out $O --seed $S --tag-prefix E10-gepa-s$S --arm gepa \
    --max-metric-calls 555 --hard-cap 600 --minibatch 3
fi
echo "exit=$?" 
$PY -I $B/code/finalize.py $M $O

budget.counted_rollouts_cap_per_search: 600 (decisions.md frozen E10 parameters; manifest/launch may differ per arm)

manifest.json.judge: azure/gpt-5.5 provider-default settings (deviation from tau2 default gpt-4.1, unavailable)
manifest.json.splits: protocol/tau_retail_splits.json (opt 49, sel 25, sealed official test 40)
manifest.json.error_tagging: candidate tools fault -> error_kind=candidate (score 0); provider/sim/judge -> infra
manifest.json.budget: 600 counted target rollouts, finalize included; chaser sel scoring is evaluation not search (tag chaser)
manifest.json.sel_note: sel is the SELECTION set, never a result
manifest.json.checkpoint: candidates.jsonl per CHECKPOINT_PROTOCOL.txt, cutoff 2026-10-13 06:00 UTC
manifest.json.infra_retry_policy: GEPA/controls: infra errors retried up to 3x, retries counted inside the budget; watchdog 7200 s (running v2 config; later launches use 10800 s, one retry, outside-budget counting). Infra-error counts to be reported at cutoff.

content.method: GEPA (gepa-ai/gepa), PyPI release gepa==0.1.4 (wheel sha recorded in wheels/), gepa.optimize unmodified
content.pin_note: GitHub main tarball download was throttled and abandoned; PyPI 0.1.4 is the released official code. Re-pin to a commit SHA if the paper needs main.
content.adapter: code/gepa_sb_adapter.py (CapEvolveSBGepaAdapter), runner code/gepa_run.py
unchanged_from_official: engine, reflective mutation proposer, default reflection prompt (InstructionProposalSignature) and its first-to-last-backtick output extractor
candidate selection = pareto (instance frontier), module_selector = round_robin, reflection_minibatch_size default 3, epoch_shuffled batch sampler
acceptance: strict minibatch improvement (sum), then full-valset evaluation of every accepted proposal; best = highest val mean
skip_perfect_score=True, use_merge=False (official default), cache_evaluation=False, perfect_score=1.0

deviations.change: evaluate() runs ONE CapEvolve SpreadsheetBench target rollout per example (patched adapter, gold-free agent view, 30 turns, podman sandbox) and returns the LibreOffice-25.8-RECALCULATED hard score (metric hard_restriction, selected by BL_REWARD_METRIC=hard_restriction in launch_e10.sh; verified in the live process environments). The as-saved score (hard_no_recalc) is recorded per rollout as reward_as_saved. [The smoke runs of 2026-10-11 early used as-saved: BL_REWARD_METRIC was unset then.]

two components {prompt.md, task_template.md} = CapEvolve's editable capability, byte-identical seed. GEPA's round-robin selector updates one component per proposal; the reflection prompt for a component does not show the other component (official behaviour).

Feedback in the reflective dataset = CapEvolve scorer's gold-safe feedback string (pass/fail, localized failure classes, no gold cell values) + the full agent transcript (<=20k chars). Official GEPA has no benchmark-specific feedback; this is the richest signal the matched evaluator offers and is also what CapEvolve's optimizer sees.

target = rits/google/gemma-4-31B-it via gateway (litellm_proxy inside the CapEvolve adapter); reflection LM = gepa.lm.LM('openai/aws/claude-sonnet-5-5', api_base=gateway, max_tokens=16000), temperature unset

official max_metric_calls is used unchanged: every example evaluation (minibatch of parent, minibatch of child, full-val of accepted children, and the initial seed evaluation on the valset) counts 1. One metric call == one target rollout. A candidate that fails the placeholder contract is scored 0 WITHOUT a model call (as CapEvolve does) but GEPA still debits its metric calls (conservative). Reflection-LM tokens are NOT part of max_metric_calls; they are metered separately via gateway tags BL-gepa-*:reflection.

rollout seed fixed to 0 for every evaluate() call (GEPA passes no seed); Gemma at temperature 0 is still non-deterministic across calls (observed: same task passes/fails across calls), so GEPA re-evaluating the parent on the minibatch (official behaviour) measures noisy outcomes
evaluate() runs batch examples concurrently (4 threads). Does not change semantics.

trainset = the 80 train ids, valset = the 40 val ids of SkillOpt's released 80/40/280 split (== CapEvolve full_verified/split_ids.json). Test ids are never passed to GEPA. Smoke runs use --val-from-train (valset = train subset) so that no val id is touched.
no merge (official default off); no objective frontier; no task-LM / default evaluator

content.practical_track_notes: native GEPA design differences from the matched track: use_merge=True (paper setting) is available via --use-merge; reflection_minibatch_size=3; valset may be the 40 val ids; budget = max_metric_calls total.

candidate selection = pareto (instance frontier), module_selector = round_robin, reflection_minibatch_size default 3, epoch_shuffled batch sampler
acceptance: strict minibatch improvement (sum), then full-valset evaluation of every accepted proposal; best = highest val mean
skip_perfect_score=True, use_merge=False (official default), cache_evaluation=False, perfect_score=1.0

deviations.change: evaluate() runs ONE CapEvolve SpreadsheetBench target rollout per example (patched adapter, gold-free agent view, 30 turns, podman sandbox) and returns the LibreOffice-25.8-RECALCULATED hard score (metric hard_restriction, selected by BL_REWARD_METRIC=hard_restriction in launch_e10.sh; verified in the live process environments). The as-saved score (hard_no_recalc) is recorded per rollout as reward_as_saved. [The smoke runs of 2026-10-11 early used as-saved: BL_REWARD_METRIC was unset then.]

two components {prompt.md, task_template.md} = CapEvolve's editable capability, byte-identical seed. GEPA's round-robin selector updates one component per proposal; the reflection prompt for a component does not show the other component (official behaviour).

Feedback in the reflective dataset = CapEvolve scorer's gold-safe feedback string (pass/fail, localized failure classes, no gold cell values) + the full agent transcript (<=20k chars). Official GEPA has no benchmark-specific feedback; this is the richest signal the matched evaluator offers and is also what CapEvolve's optimizer sees.

target = rits/google/gemma-4-31B-it via gateway (litellm_proxy inside the CapEvolve adapter); reflection LM = gepa.lm.LM('openai/aws/claude-sonnet-5-5', api_base=gateway, max_tokens=16000), temperature unset

official max_metric_calls is used unchanged: every example evaluation (minibatch of parent, minibatch of child, full-val of accepted children, and the initial seed evaluation on the valset) counts 1. One metric call == one target rollout. A candidate that fails the placeholder contract is scored 0 WITHOUT a model call (as CapEvolve does) but GEPA still debits its metric calls (conservative). Reflection-LM tokens are NOT part of max_metric_calls; they are metered separately via gateway tags BL-gepa-*:reflection.

rollout seed fixed to 0 for every evaluate() call (GEPA passes no seed); Gemma at temperature 0 is still non-deterministic across calls (observed: same task passes/fails across calls), so GEPA re-evaluating the parent on the minibatch (official behaviour) measures noisy outcomes
evaluate() runs batch examples concurrently (4 threads). Does not change semantics.

trainset = the 80 train ids, valset = the 40 val ids of SkillOpt's released 80/40/280 split (== CapEvolve full_verified/split_ids.json). Test ids are never passed to GEPA. Smoke runs use --val-from-train (valset = train subset) so that no val id is touched.
no merge (official default off); no objective frontier; no task-LM / default evaluator

content.practical_track_notes: native GEPA design differences from the matched track: use_merge=True (paper setting) is available via --use-merge; reflection_minibatch_size=3; valset may be the 40 val ids; budget = max_metric_calls total.

content.method: GEPA (gepa-ai/gepa), PyPI release gepa==0.1.4 (wheel sha recorded in wheels/), gepa.optimize unmodified
content.pin_note: GitHub main tarball download was throttled and abandoned; PyPI 0.1.4 is the released official code. Re-pin to a commit SHA if the paper needs main.
content.adapter: code/gepa_sb_adapter.py (CapEvolveSBGepaAdapter), runner code/gepa_run.py
unchanged_from_official: engine, reflective mutation proposer, default reflection prompt (InstructionProposalSignature) and its first-to-last-backtick output extractor
candidate selection = pareto (instance frontier), module_selector = round_robin, reflection_minibatch_size default 3, epoch_shuffled batch sampler
acceptance: strict minibatch improvement (sum), then full-valset evaluation of every accepted proposal; best = highest val mean
skip_perfect_score=True, use_merge=False (official default), cache_evaluation=False, perfect_score=1.0

deviations.change: evaluate() runs ONE CapEvolve SpreadsheetBench target rollout per example (patched adapter, gold-free agent view, 30 turns, podman sandbox) and returns the LibreOffice-25.8-RECALCULATED hard score (metric hard_restriction, selected by BL_REWARD_METRIC=hard_restriction in launch_e10.sh; verified in the live process environments). The as-saved score (hard_no_recalc) is recorded per rollout as reward_as_saved. [The smoke runs of 2026-10-11 early used as-saved: BL_REWARD_METRIC was unset then.]

two components {prompt.md, task_template.md} = CapEvolve's editable capability, byte-identical seed. GEPA's round-robin selector updates one component per proposal; the reflection prompt for a component does not show the other component (official behaviour).

Feedback in the reflective dataset = CapEvolve scorer's gold-safe feedback string (pass/fail, localized failure classes, no gold cell values) + the full agent transcript (<=20k chars). Official GEPA has no benchmark-specific feedback; this is the richest signal the matched evaluator offers and is also what CapEvolve's optimizer sees.

target = rits/google/gemma-4-31B-it via gateway (litellm_proxy inside the CapEvolve adapter); reflection LM = gepa.lm.LM('openai/aws/claude-sonnet-5-5', api_base=gateway, max_tokens=16000), temperature unset

official max_metric_calls is used unchanged: every example evaluation (minibatch of parent, minibatch of child, full-val of accepted children, and the initial seed evaluation on the valset) counts 1. One metric call == one target rollout. A candidate that fails the placeholder contract is scored 0 WITHOUT a model call (as CapEvolve does) but GEPA still debits its metric calls (conservative). Reflection-LM tokens are NOT part of max_metric_calls; they are metered separately via gateway tags BL-gepa-*:reflection.

rollout seed fixed to 0 for every evaluate() call (GEPA passes no seed); Gemma at temperature 0 is still non-deterministic across calls (observed: same task passes/fails across calls), so GEPA re-evaluating the parent on the minibatch (official behaviour) measures noisy outcomes
evaluate() runs batch examples concurrently (4 threads). Does not change semantics.

trainset = the 80 train ids, valset = the 40 val ids of SkillOpt's released 80/40/280 split (== CapEvolve full_verified/split_ids.json). Test ids are never passed to GEPA. Smoke runs use --val-from-train (valset = train subset) so that no val id is touched.
no merge (official default off); no objective frontier; no task-LM / default evaluator

content.practical_track_notes: native GEPA design differences from the matched track: use_merge=True (paper setting) is available via --use-merge; reflection_minibatch_size=3; valset may be the 40 val ids; budget = max_metric_calls total.

content.method: GEPA (gepa-ai/gepa), PyPI release gepa==0.1.4 (wheel sha recorded in wheels/), gepa.optimize unmodified
content.pin_note: GitHub main tarball download was throttled and abandoned; PyPI 0.1.4 is the released official code. Re-pin to a commit SHA if the paper needs main.
content.adapter: code/gepa_sb_adapter.py (CapEvolveSBGepaAdapter), runner code/gepa_run.py
unchanged_from_official: engine, reflective mutation proposer, default reflection prompt (InstructionProposalSignature) and its first-to-last-backtick output extractor
candidate selection = pareto (instance frontier), module_selector = round_robin, reflection_minibatch_size default 3, epoch_shuffled batch sampler
acceptance: strict minibatch improvement (sum), then full-valset evaluation of every accepted proposal; best = highest val mean
skip_perfect_score=True, use_merge=False (official default), cache_evaluation=False, perfect_score=1.0

deviations.change: evaluate() runs ONE CapEvolve SpreadsheetBench target rollout per example (patched adapter, gold-free agent view, 30 turns, podman sandbox) and returns the LibreOffice-25.8-RECALCULATED hard score (metric hard_restriction, selected by BL_REWARD_METRIC=hard_restriction in launch_e10.sh; verified in the live process environments). The as-saved score (hard_no_recalc) is recorded per rollout as reward_as_saved. [The smoke runs of 2026-10-11 early used as-saved: BL_REWARD_METRIC was unset then.]

two components {prompt.md, task_template.md} = CapEvolve's editable capability, byte-identical seed. GEPA's round-robin selector updates one component per proposal; the reflection prompt for a component does not show the other component (official behaviour).

Feedback in the reflective dataset = CapEvolve scorer's gold-safe feedback string (pass/fail, localized failure classes, no gold cell values) + the full agent transcript (<=20k chars). Official GEPA has no benchmark-specific feedback; this is the richest signal the matched evaluator offers and is also what CapEvolve's optimizer sees.

target = rits/google/gemma-4-31B-it via gateway (litellm_proxy inside the CapEvolve adapter); reflection LM = gepa.lm.LM('openai/aws/claude-sonnet-5-5', api_base=gateway, max_tokens=16000), temperature unset

official max_metric_calls is used unchanged: every example evaluation (minibatch of parent, minibatch of child, full-val of accepted children, and the initial seed evaluation on the valset) counts 1. One metric call == one target rollout. A candidate that fails the placeholder contract is scored 0 WITHOUT a model call (as CapEvolve does) but GEPA still debits its metric calls (conservative). Reflection-LM tokens are NOT part of max_metric_calls; they are metered separately via gateway tags BL-gepa-*:reflection.

rollout seed fixed to 0 for every evaluate() call (GEPA passes no seed); Gemma at temperature 0 is still non-deterministic across calls (observed: same task passes/fails across calls), so GEPA re-evaluating the parent on the minibatch (official behaviour) measures noisy outcomes
evaluate() runs batch examples concurrently (4 threads). Does not change semantics.

trainset = the 80 train ids, valset = the 40 val ids of SkillOpt's released 80/40/280 split (== CapEvolve full_verified/split_ids.json). Test ids are never passed to GEPA. Smoke runs use --val-from-train (valset = train subset) so that no val id is touched.
no merge (official default off); no objective frontier; no task-LM / default evaluator

content.practical_track_notes: native GEPA design differences from the matched track: use_merge=True (paper setting) is available via --use-merge; reflection_minibatch_size=3; valset may be the 40 val ids; budget = max_metric_calls total.
